How it works

Every lab has three pages.

1

Learn

The full lab: clear explanations, animated figures, a worked example and interactive tools to explore each idea.

2

Exercises

Questions from easy to challenging. Solve them on paper, then open the worked answer to compare, step by step.

3

Test yourself

Twelve multiple-choice questions with nothing to type. Each answer is explained, and your best score is kept in your browser.

The course

Seven labs, one path.

Each lab builds on the one before it, so work through them in order.

Foundations

01

Number Systems

Counting and converting between bases

Decimal, binary, octal and hexadecimal are four ways of writing the same quantities. This lab explains where they come from and how to convert between any two of them.

LearnExercisesTest yourself
02

Logic Gates

From truth tables to circuits

Eight gates, each defined by a truth table. Any circuit can be read as an expression and any expression drawn as a circuit.

LearnExercisesTest yourself

Algebra and simplification

03

Boolean Algebra

Laws, proofs and canonical forms

A handful of laws is enough to simplify an expression, and every truth table has exactly one sum of minterms and one product of maxterms.

LearnExercisesTest yourself+ 52 extra questions
04

Karnaugh Maps

Simplification by picture

Gray-code order places neighbouring minterms side by side, so that simplification reduces to drawing the largest possible groups.

LearnExercisesTest yourself

Building circuits

05

Combinational Circuits

Adders, decoders and multiplexers

Adders, subtractors, decoders, encoders and multiplexers are built from gates, and larger versions are assembled from smaller ones.

LearnExercisesTest yourself

Memory and sequence

06

Flip-Flops

Synchronous sequential logic

Feedback gives a circuit memory: its next state depends on its inputs and on what it currently stores.

LearnExercisesTest yourself
07

Counters and Registers

Flip-flops working together

Chains of flip-flops count pulses, shift data serially or in parallel, and circulate a single 1 around a ring.

LearnExercisesTest yourself
